hev/vector-cost

What your index actually costs, month 1 to month 36

Vendor calculators quote you a month you will never have. Start from the one number you walked in with — how much data you actually have — and let write amplification do the rest.

These are serverless, usage-based rates — the per-GB tiers a vendor publishes and bills you at without a conversation. Most of them will also sell you provisioned capacity, and that is usually the cheaper side of the deal for re-indexing, which is where this model spends most of its money. Read every figure here as the list price you negotiate down from.

Whole-lifespan cost at the current vendor, re-index cadence, quantization and embedding model. The only thing that changes between rows is the index shape — which is the whole point.

Next

This is a model. The measurement takes about a week.

Take a 20–100 GB stratified bite of your own corpus, build all three index shapes for real, and run your own eval set against them. You get measured write amplification instead of an assumed one, recall you can defend, and a three-year number procurement will accept.

You can absolutely run that yourself — the protocol is the point, and it's in the talk. If you'd rather not, that's the engagement.
